newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates close lower on loose liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates close lower on loose liquidity.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates ended lower on Wednesday defying a central bank move to try to mop up exessive funds in the market, dealers said.

The largely loose liquidity, brought by return of the funds to the banking system forced down the interbank rate, and the moderate mop-up action by the central bank was unable to tighten liquidity, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate closed at 5.191 percent against Tuesday's 5.308 close, with 30-day commercial paper at 5.10-5.15 percent against 5.30.
The central bank issued T$5 billion of negotiable certificates of deposit later on Wednesday to try to mop up excess money, a move a central bank official described as "slight".

A central bank official said the recent sliding trend in money rates, which had fallen into the bank's target zone of 5.0-5.5 percent after many weeks well above the target, showed the loosening liquidity condition.
Dealers noted liquidity was loosening as T$8 billion worth of NCDs was maturing this week, including T$3 billion on Wednesday, flushing the banking system with cash.
The government bond market has entered a consolidation with slowing turnover, dealers said.
They said persistent profit-taking had emerged to offset some early bullish buying that had pushed bond yields down.
The benchmark 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 5.8950-8975 percent against Tuesday's 6.0400 close.
